title: Growing pea shoots
summary: Ten to fourteen days from seed to shoots.
steps: Soak 280 g (10 oz) of untreated pea seed for 8 to 12 hours, then drain and rinse.
Spread the seed in one thick layer on the mix; they can touch.
Keep covered for three days, then give light. Harvest at 10 to 15 cm (4 to 6 in) tall, cutting above the lowest leaves.

title: Growing sunflower microgreens
summary: About ten days, harvested before true leaves.
steps: Soak 200 g (7 oz) of untreated black oil sunflower seed sold for sprouting for 8 to 12 hours, then rinse.
Spread evenly, cover and weigh down lightly for three to four days so the roots push in and the hulls loosen.
Uncover, give light, and brush off any hulls. Cut when the first two leaves are open and before true leaves appear.

title: Growing radish microgreens
steps: Sow 30 g (1 oz) of seed evenly on damp mix; no soaking needed.
Cover for two to three days, then give light.
Cut at 5 to 8 cm (2 to 3 in) tall when the leaves have opened.

title: Growing broccoli microgreens
steps: Sow 25 g (about 1 oz) of seed evenly on damp mix.
Cover for three days, then give light and a gentle fan.
Cut when the first leaves are fully open and green.

title: Growing kale microgreens
steps: Sow 25 g (about 1 oz) of seed evenly on damp mix.
Cover for three days, then give light.
Cut when the first leaves have opened, at about 5 cm (2 in) tall.

title: Growing mustard microgreens
steps: Sow 20 g (3/4 oz) of fine seed as evenly as you can.
Cover for two to three days, then give light.
Cut at 5 cm (2 in) tall. The longer they grow, the hotter they taste.

title: Growing arugula microgreens
steps: Sow 15 g (1/2 oz) of seed evenly and mist well.
Cover for three days, keeping the mix damp, then give light.
Cut when the leaves are open and about 5 cm (2 in) tall.

title: Growing red cabbage microgreens
steps: Sow 25 g (about 1 oz) of seed evenly on damp mix.
Cover for three days, then give strong light for the deepest color.
Cut when the first leaves are open.

title: Growing beet microgreens
steps: Soak 40 g (1 1/2 oz) of seed for about 8 hours, then drain.
Sow evenly, cover with a thin layer of mix, and keep under a blackout cover for four to five days.
Give light and cut when the red stems are 5 to 8 cm (2 to 3 in) tall, picking off any seed caps.

title: Growing amaranth microgreens
summary: Ten to fourteen days, in a warm spot.
steps: Sow 10 g (1/3 oz) of the tiny seed evenly; mix it with a little fine sand to spread it.
Keep it warm, around 24 °C (75 °F), and covered for three days.
Water gently from below and cut at about 5 cm (2 in).

title: Growing basil microgreens
summary: Two to three weeks, in a warm spot.
steps: Sow 10 g (1/3 oz) of dry seed on damp mix and mist; don't soak it.
Keep warm and covered for four to five days.
Give light and cut when the first true leaves show, at 5 to 8 cm (2 to 3 in).

title: Growing buckwheat microgreens
steps: Soak 150 g (5 oz) of unhulled buckwheat for about 8 hours, then rinse.
Spread evenly, cover for three days, then give light.
Cut at 8 to 10 cm (3 to 4 in), before the leaves get tough. For people only.

title: Growing wheatgrass
steps: Soak 250 g (9 oz) of untreated wheat berries sold for sprouting for 8 to 12 hours, rinse, and let them sprout in a jar for another day if you like.
Spread in one layer, cover for two days, then give light.
Cut at 15 to 20 cm (6 to 8 in) for juicing. For animals, cut it above the soil, or grow it without potting mix like barley fodder and feed them the whole mat.

title: Growing barley fodder for animals
summary: Six to eight days from seed to a feed mat.
steps: Soak 450 g (1 lb) of whole, untreated feed barley for about 12 hours, then rinse well.
Spread it 1 to 2 cm (1/2 to 3/4 in) deep in the tray. Fodder doesn't need potting mix.
Rinse or water two or three times a day with clean water and let it drain fully.
Start a new tray every day for a steady supply. Feed the whole mat when the grass is 10 to 15 cm (4 to 6 in) tall, and throw out any tray that smells sour or shows mold.

title: Growing garden cress
steps: Sow 25 g (about 1 oz) of dry seed on damp mix and mist; don't soak it.
Cover for two days, then give light.
Cut at 5 cm (2 in) tall.
